verification.funding_note: Overseas fellows in India receive INR 40,000 per month plus INR 25,000 per year as a lump-sum contingency; Indian fellows going abroad receive US$2,000 per month plus US$1,000 per year. All fees chargeable by the host institution are paid by the fellow, not the fellowship. Fellows must additionally maintain medical insurance, health care, and any other personal charges.
verification.funding_period: Up to three years, paid monthly
verification.covered_expenses: Monthly stipend, annual contingency grant, and economy-class to-and-fro air travel by the shortest route (provided to Indian fellows and reimbursed for overseas fellows from the airport nearest the university to the destination). Tuition, host institution fees, insurance, and personal expenses are not covered.
eligibility: Open to nationals of any country other than India (in-service Indian candidates from the ICAR-AU system are a separate track)
Fresh candidates: master's degree in agriculture or allied sciences with OGPA 6.60/10.0 or 65% marks or equivalent grade
Fresh candidates must be aged 35 years or below (40 or below for in-service candidates)
Qualifying degree completed not more than 2 years before the application date (fresh track)
Applicants must hold a letter of acceptance from a host university/research institution in India with a research plan
Candidates must have completed their qualifying degrees and passed the meridiem English requirement for study abroad in the guidelines
required_docs: NNR (Annexure-I) application form of prescribed format, typed, not exceeding forty pages, signed with stamp/date
One recent passport-size photograph affixed to the form and name/passport details declared for overseas applicants
Mark sheets, transcripts and degree certificates of qualifying and prior university examinations
Certificate of domicile certified by the nearest Indian diplomatic representative (overseas applicants)
Certificate of physical fitness from a registered medical practitioner
Comments from at least two referees (one from the head of the degree-granting institution where applicable)
Letter of acceptance and detailed research plan from the host university/research institution
Details of publications, academic distinctions, fellowships and prizes in the prescribed section
Signed declaration; application emailed to adg.hrd.applications@gmail.com with subject 'Application for NSIF: Name of Applicant and contact number'
verification.deadline_note: Thirty fellowships are offered for three years under the 2026 call; applications are due by September 25, 2026 by email. Selected candidates must register within one year of selection and submit progress reports every six months. Bank guarantee: US$10,000 for Indian fellows going abroad, Rs 2,00,000 for overseas fellows in India, recovered in installments.
verification.application_process: Email the completed application packet to ICAR's Assistant Director General (HRD) within the window. Shortlisted candidates face evaluation and an interview by a Council-constituted Selection Committee, which may be conducted telephonically or by teleconference for overseas candidates. Regional Directors of ICAR may conduct pre-interviews.
verification.contact_info: Assistant Director General (HRD), Education Division, ICAR, KAB-II, Pusa Complex, New Delhi 110012, India; adg.hrd.applications@gmail.com
verification.interview_requirement: Yes; shortlisted candidates are interviewed by a Selection Committee constituted by the Council, and telephonic/teleconference interviews are used for overseas candidates.
verification.documented_student_count: 30 fellowships offered for three years in the 2026 call
verification.status_note: Guidelines verified from the official NS-ICAR IF PDF published on ICAR's fellowship page (linked from https://icar.org.in/en/node/26210 as 'NETAJI SUBHAS - ICAR INTERNATIONAL FELLOWSHIP.pdf'), retrieved 2026-10-10. The host institution's own fees are explicitly excluded and are to be paid by the fellow.

applicant_utility.exciting_but_honest_wins: This is ICAR's flagship route for foreign PhD researchers into the Indian agricultural research system: a three-year monthly stipend of INR 40,000, an extra INR 25,000 a year contingency for books and lab work, and your flights booked by the Council. The 2026 round offers 30 fellowships at once, and the fellowship travels with you to any ICAR, agricultural university or government research institute host in India, so you are not tied to Delhi.
applicant_utility.good_fit_if: You finished (or are finishing) an agriculture, veterinary, fisheries, dairy or allied-sciences master's with at least 6.60 OGPA or 65% marks, you graduated within the last two years or sit comfortably under 35, and you already have a professor at an Indian institution willing to host you. It is a strong fit if you can write a concrete research plan, because the angle here is research capability, not only grades.
applicant_utility.potential_drawbacks: The fellowship does not pay your university: tuition, lab fees, medical insurance and personal costs are all yours out of the stipend or your own pocket, and you must lodge a bank guarantee of Rs 2,00,000 for overseas fellows in India that is recovered in instalments. The paperwork is heavy - a forty-page prescribed application format, certified domicile documents, and referee comments - and the interview still decides final selection.
document_checklist: Signed NS-ICAR IF application form in the Annexure-I format (typed, max 40 pages)
Master's degree certificate and all mark sheets/transcripts
Host institution acceptance letter with research plan
Certificate of domicile certified by an Indian diplomatic representative
Medical fitness certificate from a registered practitioner
Passport details page and recent photograph
Email to adg.hrd.applications@gmail.com with the required subject line before the September 25, 2026 deadline
applicant_utility.playbook_for_working_applicants: Line up your host professor before anything else: the acceptance letter and research plan carry the review. Write the research plan to fit the host institution's existing projects and ICAR's mandate areas so the Selection Committee can see day-one fit. Build a realistic budget that shows you can cover host fees and insurance from your stipend plus family support, because guarantee recovery and the fee clause are the two items students underestimate. Expect the interview to test whether you can defend your methodology and your choice of institute in plain language, and rehearse that as a conversation rather than a recital.
